summary_context_reads.text:
**Map A bonuses:** its seven support-token bonuses, from top to bottom, are snap one display card, build a size-2 standard enclosure free, gain five money, gain one conservation, gain two reputation, gain twelve money and gain three X-tokens. The first four are received immediately when uncovered and again as break income; the last three are one-time. Take a chosen bonus before or after its project's reward. On Map A the second partner zoo upgrades a card, the third hires a worker and the fourth grants two conservation. The second university upgrades a card and the third grants two conservation. Other maps use their printed bonuses.

**University tiles:** your hand limit is **three cards without the hand-limit university, five cards with it**, checked only at breaks. Other universities do not raise or lower that limit.

| University | Research icons | Reputation on acquisition | Hand-limit effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Research university | 2 | 0 | No change; normally 3 |
| Research/reputation university | 1 | 2 | No change; normally 3 |
| Hand-limit university | 0 | 1 | Raises 3 to **5** |

Take printed reputation when acquiring the university. **Only its research icons count as zoo icons; its reputation award and hand-limit symbol are benefits, not additional zoo icons.**

**The Break track.** At the start of the game and after each break, the Break token sits on the starting space for your player count. Various actions and card effects advance it toward the end of the track. When it reaches the **last space**, you call a break for everyone: the break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get **1 X-token** for reaching the last space. Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. After the break, the token returns to its starting space.

**Break procedure** (all players, in order):
1. **Hand card limit:** discard cards of your choice down to your hand limit — normally 3, or 5 with a particular university.
2. **Tokens on Action cards:** return any Multiplier, Venom, and/or Constriction tokens on your Action cards to the supply; they no longer have any effect.
3. **Association board:** return all your association workers to your notepad (active again — all tasks are again available at 1 worker). **Restock one tile of each partner-zoo continent and each university kind**, except kinds **already owned by every player**; do not add duplicate available tiles.
4. **Replenish display:** discard the two bottom cards of the display (folders 1 and 2), move the remaining cards down, and refill the display.
5. **Take income** (when multiple players take display cards, **refill the display after each player**; usually simultaneous; if effects require an order, begin with the player who initiated the break — or the affected player closest to them — and proceed clockwise):
   - a. Money according to your zoo's **appeal** (the amount printed next to your counter on the Appeal track; e.g., space 7 pays 11 money).
   - b. **Kiosk income:** for each kiosk, take 1 money per unique building, special enclosure, **occupied** standard enclosure, and pavilion adjacent to it (sharing at least one side of a space). An empty standard enclosure provides no income, but an empty special enclosure does.
   - c. All income marked with the break-income icon on your Sponsor cards and on your **activated** zoo-map bonuses (those uncovered by supporting conservation projects).
   **When more than one player receives a display card during break income, resolve those players clockwise starting with the break initiator (or the first affected player clockwise from them). Refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.** This ordering and the between-player refill apply together.
6. **Break track:** return the Break token to the starting space for your player count. Play then continues clockwise with the next player.

### CARDS action
- **Side I:** Advance the Break token **2 spaces** (you do not gain money for this). Then either **draw from the deck** — compare the strength of the slot with the table on the card and draw the indicated number of cards (maximum 3), after which you might have to discard a card from your hand (one just drawn or one already held) — or **snap**: with strength **5 or more**, instead take exactly **1 card of your choice from the display** into your hand, regardless of your reputation. Replenish the display at the end of your turn. There is no in-turn hand limit; you only discard to your limit during breaks.
- **Side II:** Advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw cards from the deck **and/or from within reputation range** (the display up to your Reputation counter), in any order, using the upgraded table on the card (e.g., at strength 5 you take 4 cards and discard 1). The display is not replenished until your turn is complete. Snapping now works from strength **3** (strength above 3 makes no difference to a snap). **On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw; the reputation restriction applies only to the side-II draw option, not snapping.** Upgrading the Cards action also lets you progress **past 9 reputation** on the Reputation track.

**Reputation spaces and rewards:** reputation begins at 1. Each display folder covers these Reputation-track spaces:

| Display folder | Reputation spaces |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2–3 |
| 3 | 4–6 |
| 4 | 7–9 |
| 5 | 10–12 |
| 6 | 13–15 |

At reputation 5 upgrade an Action card; at 8 hire a worker; at 11 gain one conservation; at 12 gain one X-token; at 13 take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; at 14 gain one conservation; at 15 gain one X-token. Each track bonus is received immediately once. Reputation 10 still requires Cards II.

**Reputation track and display:** whenever you increase reputation, advance your counter 1 step. Reaching a space with a bonus grants that bonus immediately, once. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action (reminder icon on space 10 / folder 5). If your counter is on space 15 and you gain more reputation, it stays on 15 and you take **1 appeal per remaining reputation step**. "Within reputation range" = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. After a turn in which display cards were taken: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces from the deck. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

2. **Pay the cost** (upper-left corner) into the supply. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces the cost by **3 money per continent icon on the card**. Effects that gain you money for playing the animal pay out later — you must be able to pay the full cost first.
  3. **House the animal.** Choose legal housing and meet its capacity and terrain requirements:
     - **Standard enclosure:** any animal except a Petting Zoo animal may go alone into an empty standard enclosure of at least its printed minimum size. Flip the entire enclosure to its occupied side.
     - **Petting Zoo:** Petting Zoo animals go only here.
     - **Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary:** all reptiles and some birds show an alternative special-enclosure requirement. You may choose that housing instead. Put the indicated number of supply player tokens on its free spaces; if not enough free spaces remain, the animal cannot go there. Never flip a special enclosure.
     - **Water and rock:** the animal's required adjacency applies to the chosen enclosure, including a special enclosure. Count distinct adjacent hexes: multiple edges touching one water hex count as only one; a larger water area counts only the hexes actually adjacent. Meet any printed one- or two-space requirement.
  4. **Place the Animal card** next to your zoo map, overlapping so the information at the top edge stays visible.
  5. **Execute effects:** advance your Appeal counter by the amount shown; some animals also give conservation points or reputation. "After finishing" effects wait until the entire Animals action is done; all other effects execute immediately, even before playing another Animal card (likewise effects on other cards triggered by the play). If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.
  - When playing 2 animals, complete all steps for the first (except "after finishing" effects) before the second; you may decline to play a second. Execute "after finishing" effects only after moving the Animals card to slot 1.
- **Side II:** You may also play Animal cards **from the display** within your reputation range, paying an additional cost equal to the folder number the card is on (2 animals may be any mix of hand/display; the display is not replenished until your turn ends). At strength **5 or more**, you may **optionally gain 1 reputation first**, at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies to the animals you then play. You may also play animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.

**Animal card layout:** hexagon = minimum standard-enclosure size; adjacent rock/water icons = required adjacent spaces; alternative special enclosure (with spaces occupied) shown beside it; money cost below; extra play conditions lower-left; category and continent icons upper-right (Petting Zoo animals have no continent); appeal gain (plus any conservation/reputation bonuses) lower-right; play effects per the glossary. If an effect refers to an icon that appears on the card itself, that icon counts. Some animals have an **interactive effect**, which can only apply to you if your zoo has **5 or more appeal** (space 5 on the Appeal track is marked as a reminder). Some cards carry a solo-mode replacement effect in a blue box.

- **Two separate support limits:** a reward level is available only if **no player at all** has a token on it. Each level can hold **one token total across all players**. Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free. Thus an opponent's token blocks that level too; having no token of your own on the level is insufficient.
    - **Support procedure:**
      1. Fulfill a condition on the card that has no player token on it. If you fulfill several conditions, choose one. You may support each project only once, never one already holding your token.
      2. Take one player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map and put it on the chosen condition.
      3. Gain the depicted conservation reward and any depicted reputation. Removing the map token activates its uncovered bonus: take it immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice.
      4. **Recurring bonus:** if the uncovered map bonus is marked as recurring income, gain that same bonus again in every break.
    - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
    - **Icon-count** projects: count the icons on the top edge of all your cards — Animal and Sponsor (including the water or rock space requirements, but not the conditions on the left side) — plus your partner zoos and universities. The card itself counts for its own effects; a double icon counts twice. Conservation-project icons do not count as icons in your zoo. Breeding Program projects (123–127) have the same requirement for all three reward spaces: choose any available one.
- **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

### SPONSORS action
- **Side I:** Play **exactly 1 Sponsor card** from your hand: the action's strength must be at least the card's **level**, and you must meet any conditions on the card's left side. Execute its instant effect and/or its recurring effect (if triggered by the card's own icon), then place it next to your zoo map. **OR:** advance the Break token a number of steps equal to the strength and take that much money — you take the full money even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps to reach the final space.
- **Side II:** Play **one or more** Sponsor cards:
  - **Level budget:** action strength **+1** must be at least the sum of all played cards' levels. X-tokens may push strength beyond 5.
  - **Card sources:** use your hand and/or the display within reputation range. Pay each display card's folder number as an additional cost; replenish only at turn end. Sponsors II also permits cards whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
  - **Effect order:** play the cards one after another. Fully execute each card's instant effects before the next; defer its "after finishing" effects until the action is finished.
  - **Money option:** if you instead advance the Break token, take the money **twice**.

**Sponsor card layout:** level in the upper-left corner (with any build-adjacency water/rock requirement beside it); play conditions on the left; the card's own icon in the upper-right corner. A recurring effect appears at the top on a blue background — purple if it is income in every break. A one-off play effect has a yellow background (lower-left); a final-scoring effect has a brown background (lower-right), with a vertical brown strip behind the level as a reminder once cards are overlapped. If a Sponsor card's effect refers to an icon on the card itself, it counts — but only icons in the upper-right corners of cards are used (plus the rock and water icons in the upper-left). Some Sponsor cards place **unique buildings** (from the 15 tiles) into your zoo, subject to any water/rock adjacency shown; a certain minimum reputation is required to play certain Sponsor cards.

## Special Rules & Edge Cases

- **Reputation cap:** reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action; on space 15, further reputation converts to 1 appeal per step instead.
- **Interactive effects** on Animal cards apply to you only if your zoo has **5 or more appeal**.
- **Full zoo map:** covering every space except water and rock spaces immediately grants 7 appeal (requires the upgraded Build action to reach the restricted spaces; can also trigger from other effects that build in your zoo).
- **Display timing:** whenever you take cards from the display (snap, or upgraded Cards/Animals/Association/Sponsors plays), do not replenish it until your entire turn is complete; then slide cards down folders in order and refill from the deck. **During the break, at step 4 before income**, discard folder 1 and 2 cards, compact the remaining cards and refill the display.
- **Hand size:** unlimited during play; enforced only at breaks (limit 3, or 5 with the specific university).

Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

A connected space is **uncovered** and shares an edge with a covered space. An isolated space has no adjacent covered space. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. "Your zoo" includes your played cards, map and personal supply; "any zoo" includes these for all players.

For an effect written "X : Y," **X on the left is the condition and Y on the right is the reward**. A condition without a number (or with "per") pays once per fulfillment. A numbered threshold pays only once; with several thresholds use the highest one met. Blue effects are permanent/recurring, purple gives break income, yellow is an instant play benefit and brown is final scoring.

Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor: if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate it freely, but do not flip it. Apply ordinary placement rules and any terrain requirements; no size-based construction payment is due. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals and never count as water or rock spaces.

- F: 5 appeal with a full map except water/rock.

**219 Diversity Researcher**

- I: **2 money per water/rock icon**.
- R: You may cover water/rock spaces and ignore terrain requirements of animals and unique buildings; their printed terrain icons still count. Terrain need not be covered for a full map. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo.
- F: 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, maximum three pairs.
